land.text: Cliopatria's Pomerania outline of 1187 (Bogislaw I died in 1187; the duchy 'a Danish vassal' after 1185)

predecessors.note: This dossier continues the Griffin duchy of the Cliopatria row Pomerania (1139..1187, dossier `pomerania` of eu-15-e), which says: a later dossier for the Griffin duchy 1188-1637 is needed. The orchestrator may merge the two (the same state).

land.text: 'At the Peace of Westphalia in 1648 and the Treaty of Stettin in 1653, Sweden received Western Pomerania' with Rügen, Usedom, Wollin and a strip east of the Oder with Damm and Gollnow

successors.note: The Swedes held the whole duchy from 1630; Stettin passed to Brandenburg-Prussia in 1720 (Swedish Pomerania page).

land.text: 'Brandenburg-Prussia received Farther Pomerania (Hinterpommern)': the part of the former duchy east of the Oder except Stettin

successors.note: Cliopatria's Brandenburg-Prussia shape covers it from 1648. Lauenburg and Bütow, a Polish fief, were 'granted as a fief to the Hohenzollern dynasty' in 1657 (Bromberg).

capitals.name: Stettin (Szczecin)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Stettin (Szczecin)'. The line was divided into Wolgast and Stettin in 1295-1478 and 1532, with several residences; the page names no other capital.

correction.text: the Griffin duchy as Cliopatria's 1187 outline without the Lands of Schlawe and Stolp, which the page dates to 1317

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: continues Cliopatria's pomerania_1177 (1177-1187, 26,765 km2; the 1187 outline is 28,325 km2 in the gazetteer grid). The page says the dukes were Danish vassals 1185-1227 and took the duchy as an imperial fief again in 1227; it dates the extension 'by the Lands of Schlawe and Stolp in 1317', while Cliopatria's shape already reaches 17.65E, so a 40 km circle at Stolp (16.95E 54.46N) is taken out until then. Adjust.

correction.text: after the loss of the Uckermark to Brandenburg

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'lost the Uckermark to Brandenburg' (13th century, undated; the 1250 Treaty of Landin is the page's treaty between the Pomeranian dukes and the margraves). A 30 km circle at Prenzlau (13.86E 53.32N), soft.

correction.text: with the Lands of Schlawe and Stolp (1317)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'extended by the Lands of Schlawe and Stolp in 1317'.

New keyframe: the Principality of Rügen, 'the island of Rügen and the adjacent mainland from 1168 until 1325', passed after Wizlaw III's death in 1325. Drawn as a 35 km circle at 13.40E 54.43N (about 2,000 km2). The page does not say that the whole principality came to the Griffins: it mentions two wars with Mecklenburg for the inheritance, undated.

correction.text: with the Lands of Stolp pawned to the Teutonic Order

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'The lands of Stolp were pawned to the Teutonic Order from 1329 to 1341.' A 25 km circle at Stolp.

correction.text: the duchy after the redemption of Stolp

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the pledge ends in 1341. The 1295 partition into Wolgast and Stettin (to 1464/1478) is internal.

correction.text: with the Lauenburg and Bütow Land

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 1455 Poland promised the Lauenburg and Bütow Land to Duke Eric II of Pomerania'; in 1466 Casimir IV 'again granted the towns to the Griffins', as trustees or in pawn; the dispute ended in 1526 when Sigismund I 'entrusted the area as a fief' to Duke George I. A 25 km circle at 17.6E 54.35N. Bogislaw X reunited the duchy in 1478 and it was divided again in 1532. The Swedish occupation from 1630 does not change the outline. No area is given on any page (infobox none); the drawn shape is about 31,000 km2.

ledger.note: 1188: the Griffin duchy continues. Bogislaw I, 'a Danish vassal' after the campaigns of 1184 and 1185, died in 1187 (Cliopatria's row Pomerania ends); the duchy stays under Danish overlordship until 'the Danes withdrew from most of Pomerania in 1227' and was then again a fief of the Empire.

region.text: the duchy round Stettin, Wolgast and Demmin

ledger.note: 13th century, tied to 1250: the Uckermark goes to Brandenburg. The dukes had to accept Brandenburg's overlordship in the 1236 Treaty of Kremmen (accepted by Brandenburg itself only in 1529) and the page names the 1250 Treaty of Landin between the Pomeranian dukes and the margraves; it says the duchy 'lost the Uckermark to Brandenburg' without a year.
1317: 'was extended by the Lands of Schlawe and Stolp in 1317.' The page names no previous holder; Cliopatria's shape for 1187 already reaches 17.65E.

region.text: the Lands of Schlawe and Stolp

ledger.note: 1325: Rügen. 'after the last Rugian prince Wizlaw III died in 1325' the principality passed to the Griffins (Wartislaw IV, 1325-1326, heads the list of rulers); the Duchy page dates the acquisition of 'the Principality of Rügen in 1325'. Two wars with Mecklenburg followed.

region.text: the Principality of Rügen: the island and the adjacent mainland

ledger.note: 1329: Stolp pledged. 'The lands of Stolp were pawned to the Teutonic Order from 1329 to 1341.'
1341: Stolp redeemed from the Teutonic Order (end of the 1329-1341 pledge).

1466: Lauenburg and Bütow. 'In 1455 Poland promised the Lauenburg and Bütow Land to Duke Eric II of Pomerania in return for his support'; after the Teutonic Order's defeat Casimir IV in 1466 'again granted the towns to the Griffins', 'as his trustees or in pawn'; the Duchy page dates the extension to 1455 and the infobox does not mention it. A Polish fief from 1526.

1478: Bogislaw X reunites the duchy (infobox 'Reunited under Bogislaw X: 1478'); it had been partitioned between Wolgast and Stettin in 1295 ('a partition ... that would last until 1464' on the page). Divided again in 1532. Internal to the state.

region.text: the Pomeranian duchies Wolgast and Stettin

ledger.note: 1630: Sweden. Infobox 'Occupied by Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden: 1630'; 'By the end of that year, the Swedes had completed the military occupation of Pomerania'; the Treaty of Stettin was signed on 10 July 1630.
10 March 1637: the duchy ends with Bogislaw XIV's death; the Swedes stay in the land until the partition of 1648 (Swedish Pomerania page).

10 March 1637: 'Death of Duke Bogislaw XIV: 10 March 1637'; 'the duchy was partitioned between Brandenburg-Prussia and Sweden' (Peace of Westphalia 1648, Treaty of Stettin 1653 for Sweden; Farther Pomerania to Brandenburg-Prussia). Brandenburg's claim rested on 'a pact between the two families in 1464'.

wars.name: Swedish occupation of Pomerania
wars.outcome: Gustavus Adolphus 'had occupied much of Pomerania on entering the Thirty Years' War in 1629' and the Swedes completed the occupation by the end of 1630 (Treaty of Stettin, 10 July 1630); the duchy ended in 1637 and was split at Westphalia.
wars.note: The Bogislaw page does not mention the 1630 Treaty of Stettin; the Swedish Pomerania page dates it.

certainty.note: The pages give lands and treaties, not boundaries; the outline is Cliopatria's 1187 shape with circles for the dated additions and losses.
As above; the Lauenburg and Bütow Land was a Polish fief from 1526.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (5 pages; budget 5). New state: Cliopatria's Pomerania row covers only 1139-1187 (dossier `pomerania`, eu-15-e); this dossier is the continuation 1188-1637 that eu-15-e, electorate-of-brandenburg and the group scope ask for. It could be merged into `pomerania` (same state, one colour).

SHAPES. From Cliopatria's pomerania_1187 outline (28.3 k km2 in the grid) with 40 km at Stolp (16.95E 54.46N), 30 km at Prenzlau (13.86E 53.32N), 35 km at Rügen (13.40E 54.43N) and 25 km at Lauenburg-Bütow (17.6E 54.35N). Gazetteer names wanted: 'Stolp' (Slupsk), 'Prenzlau', 'Rügen' (island), 'Lauenburg' (Lebork), 'Bütow' (Bytow).

NOT SETTLED. (1) The Schlawe and Stolp lands: the page dates their acquisition to 1317, but Cliopatria's 1139 shape already reaches them (eu-15-e says the same); the first keyframes remove them. (2) The Uckermark loss is undated on the page; 1250 is the page's treaty year. (3) Rügen came with two wars against Mecklenburg (undated on the page); the Mecklenburg share of the inheritance is not on it. (4) Lauenburg-Bütow: 1455 (Duchy page, Poland's promise) against 1466 (Peace of Thorn grant) against 1526 (fief). (5) Overlordships (Poland 1121-1138, Denmark 1185-1227, Brandenburg's claim 1236/1250/1529, Empire 1181 and 1227-1637) are vassal ties of the suzerains' ledgers. (6) Treaty of Grimnitz (1529), Pyritz (1493), Soldin (1466) and the 1569 Stettin/Wolgast division are not on any page opened. (7) 1637-1648: the Swedes held the land; Brandenburg's inheritance claim ('a pact between the two families in 1464') was settled only at Westphalia. (8) The 1295 partition into Wolgast and Stettin and the 1478/1532 reunion and division are internal and not drawn. (9) No area on any page.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: principality-of-rugen (1168-1325), teutonic-order (Cliopatria), kingdom-of-poland (exists elsewhere), margraviate-of-brandenburg (exists), swedish-empire, duchy-of-mecklenburg (the earlier state: the slug is Cliopatria's 1806-1870 row).
